input.quote: (a) In the event the Company terminates this Agreement, the Company shall pay to HDI a termination payment, (the "Termination Payment") the amount of which shall be an amount equal to the aggregate Net Sales for the twelve (12) months preceding the Termination Date less $800,000, the balance of which shall be divided by two.
input.rationale: Section 4.1 gives either Party a convenience exit on ninety (90) days' written notice against a one-year auto-renewing term, so the notice mechanics themselves sit at the playbook fallback (Customer 60–90 days; symmetric HDI right effective at the renewal date) and are not redlined. The failure is the fee: Section 4.2(a) requires the Company — and only the Company — to pay a Termination Payment equal to 50% of trailing twelve-month Net Sales above $800,000, payable in eight quarterly instalments. Because our fees are 30% of Net Sales above $11,000 per month (Section 3.1), that formula can substantially exceed a full year of fees and dwarfs the fallback cap of three months' fees, making it a penalty on a convenience exit; HDI bears no equivalent charge. That is a material failure of the fallback, so we propose the smallest fix: cap the Termination Payment at three months' Section 3.1 fees and disapply it where we terminate for HDI's breach or under the Section 1.6 launch-failure right. Our preferred position (no fee, pro-rata refund) is noted in the comment but the revenue-share bargain makes the fallback cap proportionate here; there are no prepaid fees to refund since fees are paid monthly in arrears.

proposal.summary: Cap the Termination Payment payable on a Company termination at three months' fees
proposal.comment: [Playbook] We are comfortable with the mutual ninety (90) days' notice right in Section 4.1, but the Termination Payment formula in Section 4.2(a) is an uncapped share of Net Sales that can far exceed the fees HDI would have earned, which functions as a penalty on our exit. Our playbook position is termination for convenience without penalty; as a fallback we can accept an early-termination fee capped at three (3) months' fees, and no fee where we terminate for HDI's failure to perform.

ops.oldText: the balance of which shall be divided by two.
ops.newText: the balance of which shall be divided by two; provided, that in no event shall the Termination Payment exceed an amount equal to the aggregate payments made by the Company to HDI pursuant to Section 3.1 in respect of the three (3) calendar months immediately preceding the Termination Date. No Termination Payment shall be due or payable if the Company terminates this Agreement as a result of HDI's breach or pursuant to Section 1.6.
